components.text: Intermittent particle bursts, moving air and a CO₂ signal that is not proportional to particles. Start with April 15, then narrow to 16:00–17:00 to compare 16:22 with 16:41.

Dots are recorded minute means and whiskers are observed minima to maxima, not confidence intervals. Particle scale is symlog, linear near zero and compressed at high values. Wind and CO₂ scales are linear and auto-range. No interpolation or clock shifts. Hover for local time, counts and quality notes. Coverage strips flag minutes affected by particle gaps or excluded wind samples; records present does not mean quality approved. Twelve whole particle minutes are missing within the 65-hour record; longest inter-reading interval is 73.99 s.

components.title: What these sensors cannot establish
components.body: ES-642 is an optical particle-mass estimate with 1 µg/m³ sensitivity; inlet size cut and smoke calibration are unverified, so this is not confirmed PM2.5, PM10 or AQI. CSAT3 wind excludes 256 flagged samples; north orientation and sensor geometry are unverified. LI-7200 dry CO₂ is not a combustion-specific tracer. Negative-value minutes on April 16 at 10:00–10:06 and April 17 at 09:30–09:36 are retained and flagged, not accepted as ambient air. WindObserver II, LI-840A and Picarro have no April 15 records. Unknown clock synchronization and inlet delays prevent a defensible lag, plume path, emissions factor or flux.

components.text: Particle and CO₂ extremes overlap only partly
April 15, 2022 in CDT. Only four of the ten highest particle minutes are among the ten highest CO₂ minutes. Correlation across 08:00–24:00 is 0.20, compared with 0.44 within 16:00–17:00.

components.title: Paired minute means by time of day

components.text: 958 paired minutes from 08:00–24:00; two empty particle minutes omitted without filling. Each dot has equal weight in the minute correlations. Labels identify selected peak and counterexample minutes, not independent episodes. Hover for descending ranks and particle gap flags; filter by time-of-day group to compare periods. The particle axis is symlog; correlations reported here use untransformed concentrations. Thirty-two included minutes have partial particle gaps. Removing those changes full-window Pearson r from 0.196 to 0.195. Serial dependence, shared trends, unknown geometry and clock/inlet delays prevent causal or transport-lag inference.
